- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp price spikes in history.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after high historical prices and underestimates after low ones.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually adjust downward — suggesting lag in recognizing short-term volatility.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum after sustained high prices; often holds forecasts too high for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially when true values are trending down.
- Forecasts are sensitive to recent history — if last 5–7 days are high, model overreacts; if low, underreacts.
- Model does not adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., consistently underestimates prices in late May/early June.
